routes.label: Count the two ring portions separately

question:
As shown in the figure below, a regular dodecahedron (the polyhedron consisting of \(12\) congruent regular pentagonal faces) floats in space with two horizontal faces. Note that there is a ring of five slanted faces adjacent to the top face, and a ring of five slanted faces adjacent to the bottom face. How many ways are there to move from the top face to the bottom face via a sequence of adjacent faces so that each face is visited at most once and moves are not permitted from the bottom ring to the top ring?

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_10A_Q19_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Only face adjacency matters, so think of each face as a stop and each shared edge as a possible move. Within either ring, the five faces form a cycle: each face has two neighbors in its own ring. Each upper-ring face also has two lower-ring neighbors, since its other three edges meet the top face and its two upper-ring neighbors.

Every valid route first enters the upper ring, later crosses to the lower ring, and finally enters the bottom face. There is exactly one crossing between the rings: a route must cross downward to reach the bottom, and afterward it cannot return upward. The top face cannot be used again because it has already been visited.

Consider the portion of a route within one ring, starting from a fixed entry face. It can make zero moves around the ring in one way. If it makes any ring moves, it must continue in its initially chosen direction, because reversing direction would immediately revisit the preceding face. It can make \(1,2,3,\) or \(4\) such moves, in either direction. A fifth move would revisit the entry face. Thus the number of possible ordered ring portions is
\[
1+2\cdot4=9.
\]

We can now construct a route in four stages:

1. Choose the first upper-ring face: \(5\) choices.
2. Choose its upper-ring portion: \(9\) choices.
3. Cross to either lower-ring neighbor of the last upper face: \(2\) choices.
4. Choose the lower-ring portion: \(9\) choices, then move to the bottom face.

All lower-ring faces are unvisited when the crossing occurs, so all nine lower-ring portions remain available. Every selection produces a legal route. Conversely, a legal route uniquely determines these four selections, so no route is omitted or counted twice. The total is
\[
5\cdot9\cdot2\cdot9=\boxed{810},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
